diagnosis.summary: The product-service Lambda handler is running far slower than normal, with end-to-end latency across all percentiles rising roughly 100x to 160x above baseline. No 5xx errors are present on either affected service. The payment-service shows a doubled request rate but its own handler duration and latency remain near baseline.
diagnosis.root_cause: Severe slowdown in the product-service Lambda handler body is the most likely root cause, with the handler's CPU time rising approximately 224x while end-to-end latency rose by a similar magnitude, consistent with a compute-intensive code path in the handler itself.
evidence: product-service lambda_duration_ms_mean rose from 2.49 ms to 557.78 ms, an increase of approximately 224x.
product-service lambda_duration_ms_p95 rose from 3.12 ms to 559.61 ms, an increase of approximately 179x, tracking closely with the mean handler duration rise.
product-service end-to-end latency rose across all measured percentiles: p50 from 4.09 ms to 655.06 ms (~160x), p95 from 6.56 ms to 665.12 ms (~101x), and p99 from 9.59 ms to 697.75 ms (~73x).
product-service error_rate_5xx remains at 0, unchanged from its baseline of 0.

payment-service request_rate rose from 0.94 rps to 1.88 rps, while its lambda_duration_ms_mean fell from 0.5855 ms to 0.258 ms and p95_latency_ms moved from 4.51 ms to 3.78 ms, indicating no handler slowdown in that service.
recommended_actions: Inspect CloudWatch Logs at /aws/lambda/anomalypulse-product for the current window to identify which code path in the handler is consuming the extra CPU time.

Check the CloudWatch Duration and Errors metrics for anomalypulse-product to determine whether any invocations are approaching or hitting the 10 s timeout, as those would not appear in error_rate_5xx or the latency percentiles.
If logs point to a specific recent code or configuration change on anomalypulse-product, roll back that change; otherwise fix the slow code path directly rather than rolling back on timing alone.
After any change, recheck lambda_duration_ms_mean and p95_latency_ms for product-service to confirm the handler has returned to baseline levels.
Monitor payment-service request_rate to determine whether it stabilises once product-service latency recovers.
